output.brief: The departures are concentrated in one place. Eight of the 11 associates on Kestrel have resigned, against 1 of the 13 who were never on it. Pay and the firm-wide billable-hours increase apply to everyone in the group, so they are unlikely to explain that gap. The firm-wide figures also rule out ordinary market movement as the explanation. Kestrel is not a clean comparison, though. All 11 Kestrel associates report to Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no one else. The heavy workload and his supervision therefore can't be told apart in the records. The survey comments point to both. The exit forms are weak evidence: leavers were told the group head might read them, and most gave 'career opportunity' with no detail. I'm fairly sure the problem sits in Kestrel. I'm not sure whether workload or supervision is the cause. Don't announce the £12k payment or close the review. Commission the confidential outside interviews, about £9k, with questions that separate workload from supervision. Four leavers have already agreed to take part. Ask the interviewer to cover Kestrel associates who haven't resigned as well. Add matter and supervising-partner fields to attrition tracking. Decide on contract reviewers or a change of supervisor after the interviews. The document-review phase ends in December, so the interviews need to be quick.
